chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Yunus ibn Ribat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May Allah have mercy on the one who assists his child in his righteousness.' I said, 'How does he assist him in his righteousness?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He accepts what is easy for him and overlooks what is difficult for him, and he does not burden him nor is he awkward with him. So there is nothing between it and between one coming in a limit from the limits of Infidelity, except that one enters into disloyalty, or cutting off of a relationship.'

Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Paradise is pleasant, Allah made it pleasant and aromatised its winds. Its wind is found from a travel distance of a thousand years, but he who is disloyal (to his parents), nor a cutter off of a relationship, nor a relaxer of the trousers (an adulterer), a snobbish one, will not find its wind.'

key_terms.مُرْخِي الْإِزَارِ: One who lets down his garment (in pride or adultery)

ai.seo_question: How should parents treat their children to ensure they remain righteous and avoid major sins?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the reciprocal nature of filial piety, where parental leniency—accepting what is easy and forgiving what is difficult—serves as the primary catalyst for children's righteousness. It underscores a critical theological link in Shia tradition: the physical fragrance of Paradise is inaccessible to those who neglect these specific familial duties, positioning parental mercy as a spiritual prerequisite for the child's ultimate success.
